Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Marked anxiety with difficulty leaving home, sleep disturbance, low energy, anhedonia, and social withdrawal for ~2 months, started after beginning a new job.
- History of presenting illness:
  - Onset ~2 months ago; job change with perceived stress and interpersonal difficulties at work.
  - Daily impact: dread going to work, difficulty waking, persistent worry, and perceived impact on sleep and daily functioning.
  - Sleep: bedtime ~10–11 pm; difficulty falling asleep; awake for hours; total sleep ~3–4 hours.
  - Palpitations: mornings often feel racing/irregular heartbeats, lasting minutes (sometimes up to ~10 minutes); occasional chest discomfort with palpitations; some days feel anxious about being late; episodes may wake the patient.
  - Mood: low energy, reduced enjoyment of activities; feels on edge; episodes of feeling down.
  - Suicidal ideation: denies; no thoughts of harming self; supportive family.
- Past medical history: Not provided in transcript.
- Medications: None documented.
- Allergies: None documented.
- Social history:
  - Lives with parents.
  - Alcohol: increased intake on Fridays/Saturdays; may exceed recommended limits on those days; some weekday alcohol use.
  - Smoking/other substances: Occasional smoking; no illicit drug use reported.
  - Occupation: Works for a fashion retailer; new role in head office; stress related to job; public transport anxiety.
- Family history: Mother with depression (past).
- Review of systems: Not otherwise contributory beyond symptoms described above.

Objective:
- Physical examination: Not documented in transcript.
- Vitals: Not documented in transcript.
- Investigations: None yet; planned blood tests discussed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Anxiety disorder
   - Assessment: Likely generalized anxiety symptoms with functional impairment (sleep disturbance, daytime worry, avoidance of activities); onset ~2 months, linked to new job stress.
   - Differential diagnoses: Generalized anxiety disorder; Adjustment disorder with anxiety; Major depressive disorder with anxious distress; Panic disorder (consider if episodes meeting criteria).
   - Investigations planned: Basic blood tests to evaluate potential non-psychogenic contributors to palpitations.
   - Treatment planned: Refer for one-to-one talking therapy (self-referral via NHS) focused on anxiety management; provide online resources; sleep hygiene guidance; advise to contact GP if symptoms worsen.
   - Referrals: Self-referral to NHS talking therapies; provide linkage/details.

2. Palpitations (likely anxiety-related)
   - Assessment: Palpitations described as irregular fast heartbeat occurring mainly in the morning in stressful moments; no consistent chest pain or syncope; duration minutes to up to ~10 minutes; most consistent with anxiety-related arousal per discussion.
   - Differential diagnoses: Consider cardiac or endocrine etiologies if symptoms persist or escalate (not documented as present in transcript); basic labs to screen for triggers planned.
   - Investigations planned: Basic blood tests to rule out other etiologies.
   - Treatment planned: No pharmacologic treatment recommended at this time; monitor; follow-up after test results.

3. Insomnia / sleep disturbance
   - Assessment: Sleep initiation and maintenance problems related to anxiety; persistent non-restorative sleep.
   - Investigations planned: Not applicable.
   - Treatments planned: Sleep-focused information and coping strategies to be provided; discuss access to online resources; integrate into overall anxiety management.
